Feeling nervous about getting the COVID vaccine I have a fuckton of allergies. Never had anaphylaxis but I do have a few drug allergies and I know anaphylaxis is a rare but possible side effect of the vaccine. When the time comes for me to get it, I'm really nervous about having a delayed reaction and dying when I get home or something. I think I'm going to ask if there's any way for me to hang out onsite for a little while after the vaccine to make sure I don't have a reaction, but even then, there's always the small risk that a reaction could show up a little later. I live alone. No one would be there to help me if I couldn't breathe or talk.   But I also don't want to die of COVID. So I have to do this. I know the risk is so, so small - significantly smaller than my risk of getting COVID and experiencing life-threatening complications - but that doesn't make me feel any better.   Has anyone had it yet?

What are you supposed to do if you find a car broken into?
My city has a huge problem with auto theft, burglary, and vandalism. Like, you pretty much can't own a car here without it being broken into at some point. Today I noticed a car in my apartment complex's parking lot with the window shattered, the door open, and some stuff on the ground. I felt so bad and wanted to do something, but I'm not sure if there's anything I could have done. posts.post: Do you think it's fair to say the past year has been traumatic? I feel permanently changed by everything that's happened this past year. I am exhausted. I feel bitter and angry and sad. I have never hated people the way I do now. There are times that I feel like going outside and just screaming at the sky until I can't anymore. And I feel gaslit by the people around me who want to pretend that nothing is wrong.   I'm very lucky that the events of this year haven't had a huge direct impact on me - I have a job and a place to live, my loved ones are alive. But it feels like everything else is just a giant fucking nightmare. All I want to do is sleep and pretend I don't exist. I don't think I'm ever going to be completely okay after this, even if things do someday become "normal" again, whatever that even means.

posts.post: I just started my second semester back at college and I already feel overwhelmed I'm only attending part time right now while I work part time and I already feel like I'm in over my head. I dropped out of uni 3 years ago when I realized I wasn't happy with my career prospects and now I'm trying to get an associate's in health information technology. I'm taking intro to anatomy and physiology, the a&p lab, and medical terminology. I feel so rusty. It's been 10 years since I've taken biology and chemistry in high school. Chapter 1 hasn't been too bad so far, but this is just the beginning, and I still have so much work left to do.  It's extra hard because I've been pretty depressed lately because, well, everything around me is depressing. I sleep way too much and when I'm awake my brain feels like mush. I thought starting a new, stimulating challenge would help to perk me up and pull my head out of the fog but instead I just feel like I'm staring up at a mountain of work I can't keep up with.
